title: Demand Service Rate Programs: Withdrawal and Restoration of Dispatch Privileges
content:
## When privileges are withdrawn

Dispatch privileges are withdrawn once an invoice stays unpaid beyond the tier's suspension period
counted from the day the invoice fell due, counting calendar days with the due day excluded and the
final day included, or as soon as the open balance passes the tier's credit limit, whichever happens
first.

## What a suspension does not touch

A suspended program keeps its block hours and its emergency allowance; nothing is forfeited by the
suspension itself.

## Restoration

Privileges are restored when the arrears are settled in full and the tier's reinstatement fee is
charged, and the term is not extended by the days lost.

## A program that has already lapsed

A program that has already lapsed at its term end may be restarted at the same rates only inside the
tier's restart window counted forward in calendar days from the term end date, the end day excluded and
the final day included; past that window a fresh enrollment at current rates is needed.

### Both sides of each count (hypothetical)

On a program under the Demand Service Rate Programs whose suspension period is 30 calendar days, an
invoice that fell due on a boundary day and stands unpaid on the 30th day after it has not yet reached
the suspension period, the due day being excluded and the final day included; the same invoice standing
unpaid on the 31st day is beyond it and privileges are withdrawn. The credit limit works alongside that
count and not after it: where the open balance passes the tier's credit limit on the 3rd day, privileges
are withdrawn on that day, whichever count would have come later.

On the same program, with a restart window of 60 calendar days and a term that ended on a boundary day,
a restart on the 60th day after the term end date is inside the window and takes the same rates; a
restart on the 61st day is outside it, and a fresh enrollment at current rates is needed.
